content:
maya: quick design sync — noticed a confusing state when you switch GPU pools while editing min/max. the UI currently keeps the previous values but dims them. users might think their changes didn't apply. :thinking:

alex: can you screenshot the flow? I remember an earlier convo about a ‘sticky draft’ behavior but not sure on final copy.

maya: attached mock — sequence is: open pool A, change Min 2 -> 4, switch to pool B (auto-select), min/max fields grey out and show the 4/8 values with a faint dotted outline. no explicit hint that those values are a draft for pool A.

liam: hmm that sounds risky. if the fields look disabled people might assume pool B enforces those numbers. suggestion: show a pill "Draft (applies to pool A)" with an arrow when hovering over the inputs, and keep the control enabled so they can commit or discard. :arrow_right:

rachel: +1 on the pill. also copy tweak: use "Draft changes saved to Pool A" instead of just "Draft" — clearer which pool. shorter variant for narrow layouts: "Draft · Pool A".

zoe: accessibility note — if we add a pill we need to ensure it receives focus and is announced via aria-live when it appears. screen reader should hear something like: "Draft changes saved for Pool A. Press Enter to apply to Pool B or Escape to discard." Also keyboard users need a clear way to commit without a mouse.

alex: UX question: do we want drafts to be global across the console or scoped to the current route? i.e., if someone navigates away and returns should the draft persist?

maya: proposal: scope drafts to the workspace and persist for the session (localStorage) but expire after 24h. show a small toast: "You have unsaved capacity changes for Pool A — continue editing or discard" with an "Apply" button.

liam: implementation caveat: we already have backend validations that reject min > pool_max for some pools. if user drafts values incompatible with the target pool we should surface an inline error right away instead of allowing the draft to be applied. so the pill should include the validation state: green check or red warning.

rachel: copy suggestions for guardrail messaging: instead of "Min must be <= Pool max" use "Selected Min (4) exceeds Pool B maximum (2). Reduce Min or choose a different pool." more actionable.

zoe: for aria we can use role="status" with polite live region for non-blocking announcements. for errors use assertive only for blocking errors on Apply. keyboard shortcuts: Enter to apply, Escape to discard, and Tab should land on the pill first when switching pools.

alex: thoughts on the SLO slider interaction? currently switching pool resets the SLO slider back to default which surprised Sim yesterday. should the SLO be tied to pool or to route?

maya: my take: SLO is a route-level preference (app level), not pool-level. we should persist SLO across pool switches and only reset if the pool lacks capability to meet the target — then show a warning and fallback option. Example copy: "Selected pool cannot meet Latency SLO. Switch to Higher-Priority pool or relax SLO."

liam: backend can expose a capability flag per pool; if flag=false, we show a persisted but disabled SLO with tooltip: "This pool cannot deliver the requested SLO" and an inline action "Find compatible pools" that opens the pool picker filtered.

rachel: microcopy for the pool picker filter button: "Show pools that meet current SLO" (primary), and secondary: "Show all pools". keep the filter state sticky during navigation.

maya: small UI nit — the burst toggle label reads "Allow burst" which is ambiguous. change to "Allow temporary burst (up to X GPUs)" and include an info icon linking to docs. lightweight logic: if burst is enabled in draft but target pool has 0 burst capacity, show a subtle dashed warning: "Burst unavailable for Pool B".

zoe: confirm focus order for the burst toggle -> info icon -> burst slider. they need to be in a single tab stop sequence and the info icon should have aria-label.

deploy-bot: deploy-preview generated: capacity-drafts/feature-ghost-state v14 — preview link: https://staging.redwood/preview/1746001111 (expires in 3h) :rocket:

alex: thanks all — maya can you mock the pill + toast + updated copy and we'll run a quick 15-min review tomorrow 11:00? :calendar:

maya: will do, uploading a prototype in 30.

liam: if you're prototyping, include a short script for keyboard flow testing. I'll run integration tests once the PR hits.

rachel: also add token-level CTA copy for the toast: "Apply changes — estimated cost +$0.13/hr" so users see immediate cost impact.

zoe: last accessibility check — please include a small accessibility checklist in the PR: live region, focus order, aria-labels, keyboard-only acceptance criteria.

maya: noted. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
